messages:
sam: heads-up: PR 8488 is ready for merge but bench shows a tail bump on longseq p95. can we do a quick async check before we hit the merge window?
maria: link to PR?
sam: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/8488 — edits to allocator heuristic and kv-shard placement.
cheng: running local microbench now, will post numbers in a min.
priya: tagging perf folk @cheng @alex :eyes:
cheng: raw run (dev cluster, 1k long-seq requests):
```
before (main): p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=78ms mem=6.1GB
after (PR/8488): p50=19ms p95=57ms p99=120ms mem=6.3GB
```
cheng: saw the same tail increase across 3 runs, variance ~5-8% but consistent p95 jump.
alex: oof p95 +15ms is real. any config differences? batch size, prefill?
sam: bench used default batch horizon, prefill=4. no other changes. PR alters placement so some longseqs hit different shard combos.
priya: does this regress throughput or just tail?
cheng: throughput (tokens/s) stable +/-2%. most impact at >1k tokens requests — the p95 move comes from a minority of requests hitting a hotter shard and getting slight queuing.
maria: infra-bot kicked off canary earlier on canary-7; infra-bot: canary deployment started for PR 8488 (canary-7)
infra-bot: canary logs: 2000 requests sampled, p95=56.8ms, p99=118ms, error_rate=0.02%
alex: sounds like bench matches canary. we should either: 1) hold merge and investigate placement heuristic, or 2) merge + immediate canary rollback guard and a short hold for approvals. my vote: hold.
sam: option 1 is safest. i can dig into the KV shard assignment diff tomorrow morning.
priya: if we hold, can we get a minimal mitigation? maybe increase burst tokens for those longseq routes?
cheng: short-term config tweak: bump per-shard queue size from 16 -> 24 reduces queuing, local test p95 -> 46ms (still +4ms vs main but much better).
maria: try that on canary-7 and re-sample. infra-bot: can you apply the temp config to canary-7?
infra-bot: applied runtime config patch to canary-7: per_shard_queue=24. re-sampling...
infra-bot: canary logs (post-config): p50=19.2ms p95=46.1ms p99=90.4ms error_rate=0.01%
alex: nice, that narrows gap. not ideal long-term but acceptable as a stopgap if we want to merge.
priya: need explicit approvals from @cheng and @alex if we merge with the config tweak and follow-up ticket.
cheng: i can approve if we create a follow-up issue to revert or implement a proper placement fix + add perf unit to CI for 2k longseq samples.
sam: created issue https://issues.redwood/INF-1423 — investigate allocator placement + perf unit tests.
maria: approvals: @cheng (LGTM with follow-up), @alex (LGTM w/ rollback guard). @priya can you confirm product risk ok?
priya: product ok for small perf delta if rollback guard exists.
alex: canary guard: auto-roll on p95 > 70ms or error_rate > 0.1% for 10m. set?
infra-bot: canary policy updated: auto-rollback thresholds set.
sam: cool. i'll hold merge until tomorrow 09:30 PT to give cheng time to add CI sample and to give anyone else a chance to object.
maria: noted. if no objections by 09:25 PT i'll merge with the config patch and link INF-1423. :thumbsup:
cheng: adding a perf regression test now, will post PR link.
alex: thanks all. good coordination.
sam: thanks!
